observation_summary: The application throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when processing text in HelpFormatter.findWrapPos, specifically when the calculated wrap position equals the length of the string.
hypothesis: The while loop condition in findWrapPos uses 'pos <= text.length()' which allows 'pos' to equal the string length. When 'text.charAt(pos)' is subsequently called, it throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException because valid indices are 0 to length-1.
prediction: The condition 'pos <= text.length()' in the while loop at line 937 should be changed to 'pos < text.length()'.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies the off-by-one error in the loop condition. The stack trace confirms the exception occurs at the line where 'text.charAt(pos)' is called, and the loop condition is the only place where 'pos' is checked against 'text.length()'.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a classic boundary condition error in a loop predicate. The code fails to correctly validate the index before accessing the string, leading to an out-of-bounds exception. This falls squarely under the 'Checking' category as it involves an incorrect conditional check.
evidence_used: Bug report description: The first expression in that while loop condition should use a <, not a <=.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the loop logic is part of an algorithm, the root cause is specifically an incorrect boundary check in the loop condition, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
